title: The 3-Step Work Test Before You Buy
hook_text: BEFORE YOU BUY, TURN IT INTO WORK

beats.say: Before you buy it, turn the price into hours of your work.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a price tag fluttering on a coat sleeve in a dark empty room, low angle, single sodium light.

beats.say: That simple gadget looks cheap until you count the time it takes to pay for it.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a solitary pedestrian silhouette walking past a towering concrete wall under blue hour fog.

beats.say: How many actual hours of your life does that purchase cost you?
beats.visual: Macro lens view of heavy stainless steel clock gears turning slowly in cold fluorescent light.

beats.say: Most people look at the sticker price and assume it fits their weekly budget.
beats.visual: High angle shot of a wet asphalt road cutting through an empty industrial yard at night.

beats.say: Step one. Work out your exact take-home pay per hour just once.
beats.visual: Close-up of hands typing numbers on a dark calculator screen lit by a single desk lamp.

beats.say: Step two. Divide the total price of the item by that hourly number.
beats.visual: Silhouetted fingers tapping a glowing glass table in a dim room, extreme close.

beats.say: Step three. Ask yourself if the physical item is truly worth those exact hours.
beats.visual: Wide shot of a single glowing amber practical light in an abandoned warehouse at dusk.

beats.say: That shirt isn't worth five hours in a stuffy office when you see the math.
beats.visual: Rain-slick street at night reflecting a lone red traffic light, extreme wide shot.

beats.say: Time is your only non-renewable asset, yet you trade it blindly every single day.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person walking across a vast open concrete bridge at blue hour.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a heavy iron door latch clicking shut in cold fluorescent light.

caption: Stop looking at the sticker price. Translate purchases into hours worked. #moneyrules #personalfinance #smartspending #budgetingtips
description: Learn a simple 3-step math test to price any purchase in hours worked before you hand over your cash.
first_comment: How many hours of work is your last impulse buy actually worth?

facts.claim: Translating purchases into hours worked reveals the true cost of consumption.
facts.basis: Behavioral finance principle of time-cost evaluation.

loop_map.stakes: A purchase looks cheap until you measure it in the time it takes to earn.
loop_map.big_question: How many actual hours of your life does that item cost you?
loop_map.assume: Most people assume a price tag tells the whole story.
loop_map.reveal: Dividing the price by your hourly take-home pay reveals the true time cost.
